_readme: Permanent triage ledger for App/parse_prices.py's Cattelan-format review_flags mechanism (a block the parser declined to guess at rather than risk parsing wrong). Every product name that has EVER appeared in a review flag must have an entry here recording what was found. This is the tracked follow-up list that check_orphaned_flags.ts enforces -- a fresh flag on a product not listed here fails the build, forcing triage to happen instead of being silently forgotten (the exact bug found 2026-08-06: SAN MARCO/BLUEBELL/NAHUN/REGATA/LAVANDER were flagged but never followed up, and the app kept serving accessory-only data for them for an unknown period). Add a brand's product_name to CATTELAN_FORMAT_BRANDS in check_orphaned_flags.ts when a new brand (e.g. Bonaldo) starts using --format cattelan, so its flags get tracked from day one.

_status_meaning.real_gap: The flagged block was a genuine, entirely-missing price table. Fixed by hand-transcribing it into manual_additions.json (verified against the real page image, complete row set including any pre-existing correct rows since merge_manual_additions.py replaces the whole product).
_status_meaning.partial: The main price data was already correct; only a smaller secondary table (e.g. a Cavo aggiuntivo/Accessori row) was missing. Fixed the same way as real_gap, just a smaller row set.
_status_meaning.false_alarm: Checked the raw source text (and page image where the text alone was ambiguous) and confirmed prices.json already has the complete, correct data. The flag was about some other non-price element on the page, or a row count that looked suspicious but was correct. Nothing added to manual_additions.json.
_status_meaning.known_gap: Batch-categorized (not individually page-verified like real_gap/partial/false_alarm) into one of a small set of documented root-cause buckets -- used for Bonaldo's initial 197-product seeding on 2026-08-07, where per-product page-image verification the way Cattelan's SAN MARCO etc. got would have been a multi-session effort on its own. Every instance is a SAFE flag (parser returns zero rows / skips the ambiguous row rather than guessing -- never silently wrong). Does not require a manual_additions.json entry. A future dedicated cleanup pass should convert these to real_gap/partial/false_alarm per product as each bucket gets addressed (see bonaldo_index_and_structure memory for the per-bucket game plan).
_status_meaning.missing_from_index: Added 2026-08-21 for Pianca. Deliberately distinct from known_gap: known_gap means the product IS in catalog_index.json and its price table was seen and declined; missing_from_index means the product was never added to catalog_index.json at all, so it's invisible to every check that trusts the index as the complete product list (check_coverage.ts, check_orphaned_flags.ts, etc.), not just to the price parser. Always individually verified (real page content, not just an INDICE listing) before being logged this way.
_status_meaning.superseded_reprint: Added 2026-08-21 for Pianca. A different failure mode than known_gap/missing_from_index -- not a gap at all, but a genuinely duplicate product: the SAME item (verified via exact SKU code match) is printed in two different source catalogs at two different dates, with a uniform price delta between them (e.g. a documented brand-wide 4% increase). The OLDER catalog's entry is deliberately NOT added to catalog_index.json/prices.json -- indexing it as a separate live product would present stale pricing as a current option, a real pricing-accuracy risk, not a naming/disambiguation nicety. The note must record both price points, the ratio, and the evidence (SKU match + any supporting brand documentation) so the reasoning survives if the index is ever re-derived or audited. Standing rule: code-level comparison decides supersede-vs-collision, never text similarity alone -- verbatim-identical description text can still be two genuinely different products sharing boilerplate (see 'People' under planned_disambiguation), so a supersede call always requires matching SKU codes with a consistent price ratio, not just matching prose.
_status_meaning.planned_disambiguation: Added 2026-08-21 for Pianca. Forward-looking record of a confirmed name collision (same bare name, genuinely DIFFERENT products -- different designer, different furniture type, or different code family, verified via real page content per the superseded_reprint entry's standing rule) found BEFORE the file(s) involved were extracted. Records what qualifier each colliding entry must get at extraction time (matching the convention already applied to Mambo/Eden/Levante: qualify EVERY colliding entry by source context -- source catalog when the collision is cross-file, furniture type when it's within one file -- never leave one bare while others get qualified, even if one side is already live under the bare name). Not a data problem yet (nothing has been indexed wrong), just a decision that needs to survive until extraction actually happens, so the qualifier doesn't have to be re-derived or get missed and silently overwritten at merge time.
_status_meaning.index_under_resolved: Added 2026-08-22 for Pianca. A FILE-LEVEL note, not a per-product one -- doesn't correspond to a single catalog_index.json entry, describes the current resolution state of an entire source file's INDICE extraction. Used when a file's photographic index has multiple representations at different granularities (e.g. a coarse single-row-per-category 'list view' plus a finer-grained 'card grid' view with one row per actual product) and only the coarser one has been parsed so far -- the resulting catalog_index.json entries are SAFE (real page ranges, no wrong data) but UNDER-RESOLVED (multiple genuinely distinct products collapsed into one coarse range apiece). Building the finer-grained parser is deliberately deferred as its own dedicated piece of work rather than improvised inline once a layout is only partially characterized.
_status_meaning.missing_from_index_resolved: Added 2026-08-22 for Pianca. The terminal state of a missing_from_index entry once the product actually gets added to catalog_index.json under its qualified name (as opposed to superseded_reprint, where the older entry is deliberately never indexed). The original note is kept verbatim above the resolution addendum so the discovery evidence survives; only the status changes, to reflect that check_coverage.ts and check_orphaned_flags.ts now see and check this product like any other live entry -- the ledger entry's remaining job is purely historical (why the qualifier exists), not gating anything.
_status_meaning.index_resolved: Added 2026-08-22 for Pianca. Used at TWO scopes, paired with index_under_resolved the same way missing_from_index_resolved pairs with missing_from_index: (1) FILE-level -- the terminal state of an index_under_resolved file entry once its finer-grained parser (e.g. Outdoor's card-grid parser) actually gets built and applied; the original note is kept verbatim, a resolution_note field records what changed. (2) PER-PRODUCT-level -- the terminal state of a coarse grouping's own known_gap entry once that same parser splits it into its real individual pieces, each with its own catalog_index.json entry and its own known_gap/real_gap/etc. entry below; the coarse name's OWN catalog_index.json entry no longer exists (replaced, not just relabeled), so this ledger entry is a pure forwarding pointer kept so a search for the old coarse name still finds where its pieces went, not something check_coverage.ts or check_orphaned_flags.ts need to match against a live product.
_status_meaning.reference_content_excluded: Added 2026-08-22 for Pianca (SistemiGiorno/SistemiNotte structural survey). A DIFFERENT thing from every gap/collision status above: this INDICE sub-entry was deliberately confirmed, via direct page content, to be pure explainer/technical-spec/diagram prose with no CODICI and no real price -- not a product at all, so it is INTENTIONALLY never added to catalog_index.json, not even as a zero-row known_gap placeholder. Distinct from known_gap (which means a real product's price table exists but the parser declined to guess at it) and from superseded_reprint (a real, priced product deliberately left unindexed because a newer reprint supersedes it) -- reference_content_excluded means there was never a purchasable item here to index in the first place. Each entry must record which real pages were checked and confirmed empty of pricing, since this is a scoping decision that would otherwise have to be re-derived by hand every time someone re-audits the file.

RESOLVED 2026-08-19 (dedicated hardening session, battery-first discipline): the reversed-clause-order elision silent-drop ("3er maxi and 3er all price" / "3er all and 3er maxi price" -- a real bug found via this session's own battery, not previously reported) is fixed via a symmetric mirror fallback in resolveProductQuery (variantA-resolved-but-not-variantB is now handled the same way the reverse was already handled). The 2 previously-logged bare-digit-word broadening findings ("give all online 2er price" pulling in "2-er central element"; the 3-clause tier-list case tying the whole "3-er..." family) were investigated in depth and are KEPT AS-IS deliberately, not rescored: they are the correct, safe, honest behavior per this project's standing philosophy (never confidently narrow to a single wrong answer when the query truly contains no distinguishing signal beyond a shared capacity digit -- these ARE 2-4 real, structurally different products that only share that digit). What changed instead: full_price_grid/multiple_options responses now explicitly name every distinct model_variant included whenever 2+ remain tied, so the ambiguity is visible in the message text rather than silently implied by a generic product-name label. Verified via a new 34-case dedicated battery (App/regression/check_ditre_matching.ts, wired into regression:full) covering both gaps, every prior-session regression guardrail, and new typo/multi-clause/elision-order variations -- 32/32 hard-assertion cases pass, 2 observational (documented, not asserted: 2-word elision modifiers, a non-canonical "yess" confirmation typo).

On Line Plain.note: Batch-categorized 2026-08-16 during the Shape 1/Shape 2 generalization pass across all 197 products (not individually page-verified per-product, same discipline as Bonaldo's initial seeding) -- every one of these is the parser correctly declining to guess (code detected, but no price row matched its block), not a silently-wrong row. Common pattern: a single stray accessory/sub-component code (bed-base cover panel codes ZL00X/ZT01X, carpet shade codes TAPPJTPXX, chair-leg-finish codes EXCLUSIVE/TERRA, cushion codes MIDI/CLOUD) sitting on a page whose price-table shape this pass did not verify in depth. A future dedicated pass should convert these to real_gap/partial/false_alarm per product, same as the existing Bonaldo/Cattelan buckets. Codes flagged on this product: ONLPA1A00. ALSO TRACKED: TRACKED BUG (not a per-product data gap): _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE (App/parse_prices.py) is "^\s*(?:W\s*)?[\d.,]+\s*cm" -- it requires a SINGLE numeric value before "cm" and does not match RANGE-format dims printed as "W 200-230cm" (a hyphenated low-high range, not one number). Root cause chain: _ditre_scan_sku_block walks forward from a code-header line looking for the first line whose column-0 chunk matches _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE, to know where the real price rows start. When the dims line uses range format, this match never succeeds, so the walk silently continues PAST the SKU's own real dims/price content, through the whole price grid, and into the NEXT SKU header/block entirely -- confirmed exact repro: Blum's BLUMD2000 (header text/blum.txt line 89) never finds its own dims line 99 ("W 200-230cmD 90-113cm"), the scan overruns to line 125+ and BLUMD2000 ends up carrying BLUMU1000's ("Footstool", an unrelated later SKU) price values instead of its own. Confirmed PRE-EXISTING: present in the catalog before any of this session's Ditre work (verified directly against a pre-session prices.json snapshot). Currently masked, not silently wrong in production: the misattributed values conflict with the SKU's OTHER real occurrences elsewhere in the text, so they land in the ambiguous-price safety net (shown as "can't confirm, view the page" rather than a false-confident wrong number) -- confirmed on BLUMD2000's "Customer's fabric" tier (3 conflicting values, all ambiguous=true, one of them the misattributed one). SEVERITY RISK: this safety net is fragile, not a real fix -- it depends on there being enough OTHER conflicting occurrences of the same code to keep the ambiguous count above 1. A same-session attempt at a DIFFERENT fix (reversible-dual-SKU-pair header recognition, see the "bare-code-next-to-reversible-pair" item) reduced accumulated-duplicate counts broadly enough that BLUMD2000's conflict count would have dropped to a single, no-longer-ambiguous, CONFIDENTLY WRONG value -- caught before shipping, that fix was reverted specifically because of this interaction, not because it was wrong on its own. Any future fix that reduces duplicate/repeat scanning needs to re-check this risk first. Scope, found via a catalog-wide text search for the range-dims pattern (\d+-\d+\s*cm), NOT individually verified product-by-product beyond Blum: Atlantis, Bepop, Blum (confirmed), Isla (Sofa), Isla slim, Kris Low, Kris Mix Low, Krisby (Sofa), Krisby low, Krisby mix, Krisby mix low, Melville (Sofa), On Line, On Line Plain, Sanders, Urban 2.0 (Sofa) -- 16 products total. Real fix needs _DITRE_DIMS_LINE_RE (and likely _DITRE_DIMS_WD_VALUES_RE) extended to accept a hyphenated range and decide which value (low/high/both) represents the size, verified against real rendered pages -- deliberately not attempted this session.

Freedom 2.0 sofa-bed armrests S.note: PERMANENT known_gap (same standard as every other brand's accepted triage items, e.g. Bonaldo's Geometric Table 400/Mellow 400) -- not a pending "next session" item. Root cause precisely diagnosed: the "Surcharge for Move mechanism" note is not printed in any of its block's real SKU columns -- it starts at a character position INSIDE the range of the block's own last-but-one SKU column, a few characters before that column's right edge (confirmed exact repro: freedom_20_sofa-bed_armrests_s.txt line 144, "Surcharge for Move" starts at character 216, inside column D3T0M's [144,220) range). This truncates the label mid-word for that column and bleeds the remainder into the NEXT column, concatenated with an unrelated adjacent note ("Optional bed-base cover: see dedicated section"). This is a genuine column-boundary misalignment, not a wrap-buffer trigger-phrase gap -- fixing it needs detecting/handling text that starts within a few characters of a column boundary rather than assuming SKU column bounds cleanly separate all printed content, verified against real rendered pages. Confirmed a materially different problem class from the Mix-ladder whitelist gap, the merge-granularity gap, the reversed-euro-price gap, the range-format-dims gap, and the reversible-pair-header gap all fixed this session -- none of those fixes touch this mechanism (re-confirmed via a fresh catalog-wide search after both the dims fix and the reversible-pair fix landed: still exactly the same 8 products, still 211,00 each, still missing). Safe to leave permanently unfixed: the row is silently MISSING, never silently wrong -- no fabricated or misattributed price shows in its place, and no review_flag fires for it (each product has other, correctly-captured rows for the same code, so it never crosses the 0-rows-for-a-code threshold that would flag it). Scope, confirmed via a fresh catalog-wide text search, not the original estimate: Freedom 2.0 sofa-bed armrests S/M/L/XL, Isabel sofa bed, Kanaha 2.0 sofa bed, Kanaha mix 2.0 sofa bed, Lulu' 2.0 sofa bed -- 8 products, 1 row each, all 211,00.

Stone-in.note: Pre-existing bug, confirmed NOT caused by this session's excludeUnrelatedAndClause/qWords digit-signal fixes (identical reproduction on the pre-session baseline, commit 89a4ac5, before either fix landed). Root cause: checkFamilyAmbiguity (App/server/catalogChat.ts) treats 'Stone-in' and 'Stone-out outdoor' as a reciprocal 1-shared-leading-token family (both tokenize via tokenizeLoose to ['stone',...], sharing only 'stone' -- the session-5 Puppet-fix extension's own scope). To resolve which family member a query means, it strips CONVERSATIONAL_FILLER_WORDS from the query text first -- but 'in' has been in that list since before this session, and 'in' is ALSO Stone-in's own literal distinguishing suffix (tokenizeLoose splits the hyphen: ['stone','in']). A query naming the product by its own exact name ('give me all prices for Stone-in') has its own distinguishing 'in' token stripped as filler before the satisfied-member check runs, so NEITHER family member ends up satisfied, and it falls through to clarify_product instead of resolving directly. Confirmed deterministic (not LLM-flaky): reproduces identically across repeated direct calls to checkFamilyAmbiguity itself, only visible in the live regression report when the LLM path happens to confidently resolve the product name first (this session's earlier regression runs did not trigger it, likely LLM-path variance in which queries got real calls vs. the deterministic fallback -- which resolves both products correctly, since answer()'s own topMatches/maximal path never calls checkFamilyAmbiguity at all). SAME COLLISION CLASS as two already-fixed instances in this file: Bolzan's 'Bend-e Fabric' vs tier 'E' (App/server/catalogChat.ts:355) and Bolzan's 'Poltrona e accessori Flag' vs tier 'E' (App/server/catalogChat.ts:2225) -- both were fixed by stripping the product's own name from the query before filler/tier matching runs; checkFamilyAmbiguity's OWN filler-strip has no equivalent guard yet. Deliberately NOT fixed this session -- explicitly deferred to a dedicated session, same reasoning as the short-token variant-narrowing and UI-request items, given three other investigations already landed tonight. Real, fixable root cause identified (a word in CONVERSATIONAL_FILLER_WORDS should not be treated as filler when it is ALSO the chosen family member's own distinguishing suffix) -- not a case of genuinely unparseable/unfixable data.
